cues.en: So in college,
cues.zh: 所以上大学时，

cues.en: I was a government major, which means I had to write a lot of papers.
cues.zh: 我的专业是政府管理，这意味着我得写大量的论文。

cues.en: Now, when a normal student writes a paper, they might spread the work out a little like this.
cues.zh: 现在，当一个正常的学生写论文时，他们可能会把工作分散开来，大概像这样。

cues.en: So, you know,
cues.zh: 所以，你知道的，

cues.en: you get started maybe a little slowly, but you get enough done in the first week that with some heavier days later on, everything gets done and things stay civil.
cues.zh: 你可能开始得有点慢，但在第一周完成了足够的工作，随着后面几天的工作量增加，一切都能完成，事情也还能控制。

cues.en: And I would wanna do that like that. That would be the plan. I would,
cues.zh: 我本来也想那样做。计划本来是这样的。我本来，

cues.en: I would have it all ready to go, but then then then, actually, the paper would come along, and then I would kinda do this.
cues.zh: 我都准备好了，但接着，实际上论文来了，然后我就会变成这样。

cues.en: And that would happen every single paper.
cues.zh: 每一篇论文都是如此。

cues.en: But then came my 90 page senior thesis, a paper you're supposed to spend a year on. I knew for a paper like that, my normal workflow was not an option. It was way too big a project. So I planned things out, I decided it kinda had to go something like this. This is how the year would go. So I'd start off light,
cues.zh: 但后来迎来了我那90页的毕业论文，一篇你得花一年时间去写的论文。我深知对于这样的论文，我平时的工作流程是行不通的。这个项目实在太大了。所以我做好了规划，我决定它大概得是这样的。这一年应该这么过。所以我先轻松起步，

cues.en: and I'd bump it up in the middle months.
cues.zh: 然后在中间几个月加大力度。

cues.en: And then at the end, I would kick it up into high gear, just like a little staircase. How hard can it be to just walk up the stairs?
cues.zh: 最后，我再火力全开，就像一个小楼梯一样。走走台阶能有多难？

cues.en: No big deal. Right?
cues.zh: 没什么大不了的。对吧？

cues.en: But then the funniest thing happened. Those first few months,
cues.zh: 但随后最好笑的事情发生了。最初的几个月，

cues.en: they came and went, and I I couldn't quite do stuff. So we had an awesome new revised plan.
cues.zh: 转眼就过去了，而我 却什么也写不出来。所以我们有了一个超棒的新修改计划。

cues.en: And then
cues.zh: 然后呢，

cues.en: but then those middle months actually went by,
cues.zh: 但接着中间的几个月居然也飞逝而过，

cues.en: and I didn't really write words.
cues.zh: 而我实际上根本没写出什么字来。

cues.en: And so we were here.
cues.zh: 我们就这样来到了这里。

cues.en: And then two months turned into one month, which turned into two weeks. And one day, woke up
cues.zh: 接着两个月变成了一个月，一个月又缩短到两周。直到有一天，

cues.en: with three days until the deadline,
cues.zh: 距离截稿只剩三天，

cues.en: still not having written a word. And so I did the only thing I could.
cues.zh: 我却一个字都还没写。于是我做了我唯一能做的事。

cues.en: I wrote 90 pages over seventy two hours, pulling not one but two all nighters. Humans are not supposed to pull two all nighters.
cues.zh: 我在 72 小时里写了 90 页，连续熬了不止一个，而是两个通宵。人类本来就不该连熬两个通宵。

cues.en: Sprinted across campus,
cues.zh: 我一路狂奔冲过校园，

cues.en: dove in slow motion,
cues.zh: 以慢动作飞身一跃，

cues.en: and got it in just at the deadline. I thought that was the end of everything. But a week later, I get a call,
cues.zh: 在截止时间前千钧一发地交了上去。我以为这一切都结束了。但一周后，我接到一个电话，

cues.en: and it's the school.
cues.zh: 是学校打来的。

cues.en: And they say, is this Tim Urban? And I say, yeah. They say, we need to talk about your thesis.
cues.zh: 他们说，你是 Tim Urban 吗？我说，对啊。他们说，我们需要谈谈你的毕业论文。

cues.en: And I say, okay.
cues.zh: 我说，行。

cues.en: And they say,
cues.zh: 他们说，

cues.en: it's the best one we've ever seen.
cues.zh: 这是我们见过写得最好的。

cues.en: That did not happen.
cues.zh: 其实根本没这回事。

cues.en: It was a very,
cues.zh: 那是一篇非常、

cues.en: very bad thesis.
cues.zh: 非常糟糕的论文。

cues.en: I
cues.zh: 我

cues.en: just
cues.zh: 只是

cues.en: wanted to enjoy that one moment when all of you thought, this guy is amazing.
cues.zh: 想享受刚才那一刻，让大家觉得这人太牛了。

cues.en: No. No. It was very, very bad.
cues.zh: 并没有。真没有。它真的很烂很烂。

cues.en: Anyway,
cues.zh: 总之，

cues.en: today I'm a writer, blogger guy. I write the blog Wait But Why.
cues.zh: 我今天是个写作者、博客博主。我写 Wait But Why 这个博客。

cues.en: And a couple years ago, I decided to write about procrastination.
cues.zh: 几年前，我决定写一篇关于拖延症的文章。

cues.en: My behavior has always perplexed the nonprocrastinators
cues.zh: 我的行为一直让周围的

cues.en: around me, and I wanted to explain to the nonprocrastinators
cues.zh: 非拖延症患者感到困惑，我想向这个世界的非拖延症患者

cues.en: of the world
cues.zh: 解释一下，

cues.en: what goes on in the heads of procrastinators and why we are the way we are. Now, I had a hypothesis
cues.zh: 拖延症患者的脑袋里究竟在想什么，以及我们为什么会这样。当时我有一个假设，

cues.en: that the brains of procrastinators were actually different than the brains of other people.
cues.zh: 即拖延症患者的大脑其实和其他人的大脑不一样。

cues.en: And to test this, I found an MRI lab that actually let me scan both my brain and the brain of a proven nonprocrastinator,
cues.zh: 为了验证这一点，我找了一家 MRI 实验室，让我扫描了我的大脑和一个公认的非拖延症患者的大脑，

cues.en: and I... And so I could compare them, and I actually brought them here to show you today. And I want you to take a look carefully to see if you can notice And I know that if you're not a trained brain expert, it's not that obvious, but just take a look. Okay? So here's the brain of a non procrastinator.
cues.zh: 然后我……所以我可以对比一下，我今天把它们带到这里来展示给大家。我想请大家仔细看看，能不能看出……我知道如果大家不是受过专业训练的大脑专家，这并不那么明显，但还是看一眼。好吧？这就是那个非拖延症患者的大脑。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: here's my brain.
cues.zh: 这就是我的大脑。

cues.en: There is a difference.
cues.zh: 这其中是有区别的。

cues.en: Both brains have a rational decision maker in them, but the procrastinator's
cues.zh: 两个大脑里都有一个理性的决策者，但拖延者的

cues.en: brain also has an instant gratification
cues.zh: 大脑里还有一个及时行乐的

cues.en: monkey. What does this mean for the procrastinator? Well, means everything's fine until this happens.
cues.zh: 猴子。这对拖延者意味着什么？嗯，意味着一切都好，直到这件事发生。

cues.en: So the rational decision maker will make the rational decision to do something productive,
cues.zh: 所以理性的决策者会做出做点有成效的事的理性决定，

cues.en: but the monkey doesn't like that plan. So he actually takes the wheel, and he says, actually, let's read the entire Wikipedia page of the Nancy Kerrigan, Tanya Harding scandal, because I just remembered that that happened.
cues.zh: 但猴子不喜欢这个计划。所以它实际上接管了方向盘，并且说，其实，让我们把南希·克里根和托尼娅·哈丁丑闻的整个维基百科页面都读一遍吧，因为我刚想起来这事发生过。

cues.en: Then
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: then we're going go over to the fridge. We're going see if there's anything new in there since ten minutes ago.
cues.zh: 然后我们要去冰箱那里。我们要看看里面有没有什么从十分钟前开始的新东西。

cues.en: After that,
cues.zh: 在这之后，

cues.en: we're going go on a YouTube spiral that starts with videos of Richard Feynman talking about magnets and ends much, much later with us watching interviews with Justin Deeper's mom.
cues.zh: 我们要开启一段 YouTube 连环浏览，从理查德·费曼谈论磁铁的视频开始，在很久很久以后以我们观看贾斯汀·比伯（注：原文发音谐音）妈妈的采访结束。

cues.en: All of that's going to take a while, so we're not going to really have room on the schedule for any work today. Sorry.
cues.zh: 所有这些都要花上一段时间，所以我们今天在日程表上真的腾不出空间来工作了。抱歉。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: what is going on here?
cues.zh: 这到底是是怎么回事？

cues.en: The instant gratification monkey does not seem like a guy you want behind the wheel. He lives entirely in the present moment. He has no memory of the past, no knowledge of the future, and he only cares about two things, easy and fun.
cues.zh: 及时行乐的猴子看起来可不是你想让它掌舵的那种家伙。它完全活在当下。它没有对过去的记忆，没有对未来的认知，并且它只关心两件事，简单和有趣。

cues.en: Now, in the animal world,
cues.zh: 然而在动物世界里，

cues.en: that works fine. If you're a dog and you spend your whole life doing nothing other than easy and fun things, you're a huge success.
cues.zh: 这套行得通。如果你是一只狗，你的一生除了简单和有趣的事什么都不做，那你就是个巨大成功。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: to the monkey,
cues.zh: 给猴子，

cues.en: humans are just another animal species. He has to keep well slept, well fed, and propagating into the next generation,
cues.zh: 人类只是另一种动物物种。他必须睡好、吃好，并繁衍到下一代，

cues.en: which in tribal times might have worked okay. But if you haven't noticed, now we're not in tribal times. We're in an advanced civilization,
cues.zh: 这在部落时代或许还行得通。但如果你没注意到，我们现在已经不在部落时代了。我们身处一个先进的文明社会，

cues.en: and the monkey does not know what that is, which is why we have another guy in our brain, the rational decision maker,
cues.zh: 而猴子并不知道那是什么，所以我们大脑里还有另一个人，也就是理性决策者，

cues.en: who gives us the ability to do things no other animal can do. We can visualize the future. We can see the big picture.
cues.zh: 它赋予我们做其他动物做不到的事的能力。我们能想象未来，也能看清全局。

cues.en: We can make long term plans. And he wants to take all of that into account,
cues.zh: 我们可以制定长期计划，而他希望把这一切都考虑进去。

cues.en: and he wants to just have us do whatever makes sense to be doing right now. Now sometimes it makes sense to be doing things that are easy and fun, like when you're having dinner going to bed or enjoying well or in leisure time. That's why there's an overlap. Sometimes they agree.
cues.zh: 他只想让我们做眼下最合理的事情。有时候，做些轻松有趣的事确实很合理，比如吃晚餐、去睡觉，或是享受闲暇时光。这就是为什么它们会有重合，有时双方的想法是一致的。

cues.en: But other times, it makes much more sense to be doing things
cues.zh: 但有些时候，动手做事情要有意义得多

cues.en: that are harder and less pleasant for the sake of the big picture, and that's when we have a conflict.
cues.zh: 为了大局去做那些更难、更不愉快的事，这时就会产生冲突。

cues.en: And for the procrastinator,
cues.zh: 而对于拖延症患者来说，

cues.en: that conflict tends to end a certain way every time, leaving him spending a lot of time in this orange zone,
cues.zh: 那种冲突每次往往都会以某种方式收场，结果让他大量时间都待在这个橙色区域里，

cues.en: an easy and fun place that's entirely out of the makes sense circle. I call it the dark playground.
cues.zh: 一个轻松有趣、完全脱离理智范围的地方，我称之为“暗黑游乐场”。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 请提供需要翻译的英文字幕。

cues.en: the dark playground is a place that all of you procrastinators out there know very well.
cues.zh: 黑暗游乐场是所有拖延症患者都非常熟悉的地方。

cues.en: It's where leisure activities happen at times when leisure activities are not supposed to be happening.
cues.zh: 这里是本不该进行休闲活动的时候，却偏偏在进行休闲活动的地方。

cues.en: The fun you have in the dark playground isn't actually fun because it's completely unearned, the air is filled with guilt, dread, anxiety, self hatred, all those good procrastinator feelings.
cues.zh: 你在黑暗游乐场里获得的快乐其实并不是真正的快乐，因为这完全是不劳而获的，空气中弥漫着内疚、恐惧、焦虑、自我厌恶，所有这些拖延者专属的美妙感受。

cues.en: And the question is, in this situation, with the monkey behind the wheel, how does the procrastinator ever get himself over here to this blue zone, a less pleasant place but where really important things happen?
cues.zh: 问题是，在这种情况下，当猴子在掌控方向盘时，拖延者究竟如何才能把自己带到这边这个蓝色区域——一个虽不那么愉快，但真正重要的事情会发生的地方？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 好吧，

cues.en: turns out that the procrastinator
cues.zh: 事实证明，拖延者

cues.en: has a guardian angel, someone who's always looking down on him and watching over him in his darkest moments, someone called the panic monster.
cues.zh: 有一个守护天使，一个在他最黑暗的时刻总是在俯视和守护着他的人，一个被称为恐慌怪兽的家伙。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: the panic monster is dormant most of the time,
cues.zh: 恐慌怪兽大部分时间都在沉睡，

cues.en: but he suddenly wakes up anytime a deadline gets too close or there's danger of public embarrassment,
cues.zh: 但每当截止日期临近，或者面临当众出丑的危险、

cues.en: a career disaster, or some other scary consequence.
cues.zh: 职业灾难或其他可怕后果时，他就会突然醒来。

cues.en: And importantly, he's the only thing that the monkey is terrified of. Now,
cues.zh: 重要的是，他是这只猴子唯一感到害怕的东西。话说回来，

cues.en: he became very relevant in my life pretty recently
cues.zh: 他最近在我的生活中变得非常重要，

cues.en: because people of TED reached out to me about six months ago and invited me to do a TED Talk.
cues.zh: 因为 TED 的负责人大约在六个月前联系了我，邀请我做一次 TED 演讲。

cues.en: Now, of course, I said yes. It's always been a dream of mine to have done a TED Talk in the past.
cues.zh: 当然，我答应了。我一直以来的梦想就是“过去已经做过一次 TED 演讲”。

cues.en: But in the middle of all this excitement, the rational decision maker seemed to have something else in his mind. He was saying, are we clear on what we just accepted?
cues.zh: 但在所有这些兴奋之中，理性决策者似乎在盘算着别的事情。他在说，我们对刚刚接受的事情搞清楚状况了吗？

cues.en: Do we do we get what's going to be now happening one day in the future? We need to sit down and work on this right now. And the monkey said, totally agree, but also let's just open Google Earth, and let's zoom into the bottom of India, like 200 feet above the ground, and we're going scroll up for two and a half hours till we get to the top of the country so we can get a better feel for India.
cues.zh: 我们能知道未来某天会发生什么吗？我们现在就得坐下来动手做这件事。猴子说：完全同意，不过我们先打开 Google Earth，放大到印度最南端，离地面大概 200 英尺，然后往上滚动两个半小时，一直到印度最北端，好更直观地感受一下印度。

cues.en: So that's what we did that day.
cues.zh: 那天我们就这么干了。

cues.en: As six months turned into four and then two and then one, the people of TED decided to release the speakers. And I opened up the website, and there was my face staring right back at me, and guess who woke up?
cues.zh: 当六个月变成四个月，再变成两个月，最后变成一个月时，TED 的人决定公布演讲者名单。我打开网站，我的脸正盯着我看，猜猜谁醒了？

cues.en: So the panic monster starts losing his mind, and a few seconds later, the whole system's in mayhem.
cues.zh: 于是恐慌怪兽开始失控，几秒钟后，整个系统一片混乱。

cues.en: And the monkey, you remember, he's terrified of the panic monster. Boom. He's up the tree.
cues.zh: 而那只猴子，你还记得，它特别怕恐慌怪兽。砰，它蹿上树了。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: finally, the rational decision maker can take the wheel, and I can start working on the talk. Now, the panic monster explains
cues.zh: 最后，理性决策者终于能接管方向盘，我也能开始准备演讲了。现在，恐慌怪兽解释了

cues.en: all kinds of
cues.zh: 各种

cues.en: pretty insane procrastinated behavior, like how someone like me could spend two weeks unable
cues.zh: 相当离谱的拖延行为，比如像我这样的人能花上两周，却无法

cues.en: to start the opening sentence of a paper
cues.zh: 开始写论文的第一句话

cues.en: and then miraculously find the unbelievable work ethic to stay up all night and write eight pages.
cues.zh: 然后又能奇迹般地拿出难以置信的敬业精神，熬一整夜写完八页。

cues.en: And this entire situation with the three characters, this is the procrastinator's
cues.zh: 而这整个涉及三个角色的情况，就是拖延者的

cues.en: system.
cues.zh: 系统。

cues.en: It's not pretty, but in the end,
cues.zh: 它不漂亮，但最终，

cues.en: it works. And this is what I decided to write about on the blog just a couple years ago. Now when I did,
cues.zh: 它奏效了。这就是我几年前决定在博客里写的内容。后来我真写了，

cues.en: I was amazed by the response. Literally thousands of emails came in from all different kinds of people from all over the world doing all different kinds of things.
cues.zh: 反响让我震惊。成千上万封邮件从世界各地、各种各样的人那里涌来，他们做着各种各样的事。

cues.en: These were people who were nurses and bankers and painters and engineers and lots and lots of PhD students.
cues.zh: 这些人有护士、银行职员、画家、工程师，还有一大批博士生。

cues.en: They were all writing saying the same thing. I have this problem too.
cues.zh: 他们写来的信都在说同一件事：我也遇到了这个问题。

cues.en: But what struck me was the contrast between the light tone of the post
cues.zh: 但让我感到震惊的是，帖子轻松的语调

cues.en: and the heaviness of these emails.
cues.zh: 与这些邮件沉重的语气形成了鲜明对比。

cues.en: These people
cues.zh: 这些人

cues.en: were writing with intense frustration about what procrastination had done to their lives, about what this monkey had done to them.
cues.zh: 带着极度的沮丧，讲述拖延症对他们生活造成的破坏，讲述这只猴子对他们做过的事。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: I thought about this, and I said, well, if the procrastinator system works, then what's going on? Why are all these people in such a dark place? Well, turns out that there's two kinds of procrastination.
cues.zh: 我思考了这件事，心想，既然拖延系统会起作用，那究竟是怎么回事？为什么所有这些人都会陷入如此黑暗的境地？原来，拖延症有两种。

cues.en: Everything I've talked about today, the examples I've given, they all have deadlines. And when there's deadlines, the effects of procrastination are contained
cues.zh: 我今天讲的一切、举过的例子，它们都有截止日期。而有了截止日期，拖延的影响就会被限制

cues.en: to the short term because the panic monster gets involved. But there's a second kind of procrastination
cues.zh: 在短期内，因为恐慌怪兽介入了。但还有第二种拖延症

cues.en: that happens in situations when there is no deadline. So if you wanted to have a career where you want to be a self starter, something in the arts, something entrepreneurial,
cues.zh: 发生在没有截止日期的情境中。所以，如果你想追求一种需要主动性的职业，比如艺术领域的某行、创业，

cues.en: there's no deadlines on those things at first because nothing's happening at first, not until you've gone out and done the hard work to get some momentum, to get things going. There's also all kinds of important things outside of your career that don't involve any deadlines, seeing your family or exercising and taking care of your health,
cues.zh: 这些事情一开始是没有截止日期的，因为一开始什么都不会发生，除非你走出去，付出艰苦的努力去积蓄势头，让事情运转起来。此外，生活中还有各种各样与职业无关、且没有截止日期的重要事情，比如看望家人、锻炼身体、照顾健康，

cues.en: working on your relationship, or getting out of a relationship that isn't working.
cues.zh: 经营你的恋爱关系，或者从一段失败的感情中解脱出来。

cues.en: Now if the procrastinator's only mechanism
cues.zh: 现在，如果拖延症患者完成这些难事的唯一机制

cues.en: of doing these hard things is the panic monster, that's a problem, because in all of these nondeadline situations,
cues.zh: 就是恐慌怪兽，那就出问题了，因为在所有这些没有截止日期的情境下，

cues.en: the panic monster doesn't show up. He has nothing to wake up for. So the effects of procrastination, they're not contained. They just extend outward
cues.zh: 恐慌怪兽根本不会出现。它没有需要醒来的理由。所以拖延带来的影响是无法控制的。它们只会无休止地

cues.en: forever.
cues.zh: 向外蔓延。

cues.en: And it's this long term kind of procrastination
cues.zh: 而且这种长期的拖延

cues.en: that's much less visible and much less talked about than the funnier, short term, deadline based kind. It's usually suffered quietly
cues.zh: 比那种更有趣、短期的、基于截止日期的拖延更不引人注目，也更少被人提及。人们通常是在安静和

cues.en: and privately,
cues.zh: 私密中承受着它，

cues.en: and it can be the source of a huge amount of long term unhappiness
cues.zh: 而它可能会成为产生大量长期不快乐

cues.en: and regrets.
cues.zh: 和遗憾的根源。

cues.en: And I thought, you know, that's why these people are emailing, and that's why they're in such a bad place.
cues.zh: 我想，你知道的，这就是为什么这些人会发邮件，也是为什么他们的处境会这么糟糕。

cues.en: It's not that they're cramming for some project.
cues.zh: 并不是因为他们在临时抱佛脚赶什么项目。

cues.en: It's that long term procrastination has made them feel like a spectator at times in their own lives.
cues.zh: 而是长期拖延让他们在有时觉得自己就像自己生活中的旁观者。

cues.en: You know, the frustration was not that they couldn't achieve their dreams, it's that they weren't even able to start chasing them.
cues.zh: 你知道，这种挫败感不是因为他们无法实现梦想，而是他们甚至无法开始去追逐梦想。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: I read these emails, I had a little bit of an epiphany
cues.zh: 我读着这些邮件，有了一种顿悟，

cues.en: that
cues.zh: 那就是

cues.en: I don't think nonprocrastinators
cues.zh: 我认为根本没有

cues.en: exist.
cues.zh: 不拖延的人。

cues.en: That's right. I think all of you are procrastinators.
cues.zh: 没错。我觉得在座的各位都是拖延症患者。

cues.en: You might not all be a mess,
cues.zh: 你们可能不像我们中的某些人那样

cues.en: like some of us,
cues.zh: 一团糟，

cues.en: and some of you may have a healthy relationship with deadlines.
cues.zh: 你们当中有些人可能和截止日期保持着健康的紧密关系。

cues.en: But remember, the monkey's sneakiest
cues.zh: 但记住，猴子最狡猾的

cues.en: trick is when the deadlines aren't there.
cues.zh: 把戏就是在没有截止日期的时候出现。

cues.en: Now I wanna show you one last thing.
cues.zh: 现在我想给你们看最后一样东西。

cues.en: I call this a life calendar.
cues.zh: 我把它叫做人生日历。

cues.en: That's one box for every week
cues.zh: 九十年人生的

cues.en: of a ninety year life.
cues.zh: 每个星期对应一个格子。

cues.zh: 格子其实没那么多，

cues.en: especially since we've already used a bunch of those.
cues.zh: 特别是考虑到我们已经用掉不少了。

cues.en: So I think we need to all take a long, hard look at that calendar.
cues.zh: 所以我觉得我们都需要好好审视一下这张日历。

cues.en: We need to think about what we're really procrastinating on, because everyone is procrastinating on something in life.
cues.zh: 我们需要想想自己到底在拖延什么，因为每个人在生活中都有所拖延。

cues.en: We need to stay aware of the instant gratification monkey.
cues.zh: 我们需要时刻警惕及时行乐这只猴子。

cues.en: That's a job for all of us.
cues.zh: 这是我们每个人的任务。

cues.en: And because there's not that many boxes on there, it's a job that should probably start today.
cues.zh: 而且因为上面的格子没那么多，这项任务或许今天就该开始。

cues.zh: 好吧，

cues.en: maybe not today, but,
cues.zh: 也许不是今天，但是，

cues.zh: 你知道的，
